newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia mazut trade in fog over likely export curbs.
newsitem.headline: Russia mazut trade in fog over likely export curbs.

text.p: Russia-based heavy fuel oil (mazut) traders said on Friday that they were expecting some form of export curb this season, but said Moscow had not yet taken any definite decisions to restrict deliveries.

"Half the people in the industry say there is a decree retroactive to November 1 but that they are actively trading; the other half say there is no decree and that they are actively trading," said one senior Russian trade source.

"It is safe to say right now that a decree (limiting exports) is a proposal, not a reality -- but remember, Russia has every year done something (to curb exports) so that it has First Deputy Economy Minister Jakov Urinson, echoing vague statements made by other government officials, said during a break in a news conference that restrictions were in the works but could not specify when or how.
"We will restrict (mazut) exports, but not via quotas," he said, declining to be more specific.

The lack of clarity has fuelled market talk based more on uncertainties than facts, with some trade sources speculating that rail tariffs for mazut transport would be raised by 40 percent on January 1, 1997.
Other traders said they expected an export duty of up to 80,000 roubles per tonne to be slapped on sometime in January, possibly retroactively to previous months.
"The only figure that's been discussed is 80,000 but a lot of (government) people are against it," said a source at Rosnefteimpex, one of Russia's largest exporters of oil products.
"We expect a decision sometime in January and we think reason will triumph."
Sources said various ministries and cabinet members had been wrangling over the issue since mid-October but had failed to reach a consensus.
Any restrictions will most likely come in the form of a decree signed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

His press office, as well as the State Customs Committee, Railways Ministry press service and Federal Energy Commission, a state body dealing with tariff issues, said they had not received any information detailing any possible export curbs.
Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov told Reuters in September an export tariff would be levied but declined to provide details.

Russia raised the export tariff on mazut to 16 Ecus per tonne from six Ecus from December 1995 to March 1996 to curb deliveries abroad. It banned exports of mazut outright from December 1994 to April 1995 over fears of shortfalls at home.
